subject: Private deployment: access boundaries, customer keys, and operator controls
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@medicorp.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medicorp.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on private deployment boundaries and customer keys

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we dig into procurement, our security and legal teams want written confirmation on a few items specific to a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment:

- Who holds the master CMKs in each deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? We need the option that the customer retains sole control.
- For private deployments, can you provide a clear matrix of what Redwood operators can see (logs, metrics, payloads) and the conditions under which support engineers may access anything?
- Is there an operator break-glass process, and can you share artefacts (audit trail, approval flow) we can reference in the DPA?
- Any data transfer or subprocessors we should be aware of for on-prem connectors (e.g., backup mirrors, telemetry collectors)?

We prefer short-form answers so we can attach to our SOW/DPA.

Appreciate it — Alice
Information Security, MediCorp

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@medicorp.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment boundaries and customer keys

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and attaching a short matrix + DPA clause draft for reference.

1) Master keys: For private deployments (VPC/on-prem) the customer can provision and retain their CMKs (BYOK). Redwood supports CMK import/wrapping with customer KMS; Redwood never persists the unencrypted master key. For hosted API we control key material.

2) Operator visibility: See attached "privdep_operator_matrix.pdf" but summary:
   - System telemetry (host health, GPU metrics): visible to Redwood operators, aggregated and not application payloads.
   - Application payloads (request/response content): not logged by default in private deployments; we offer an opt-in debug capture that encrypts artifacts with customer CMK and is retained per retention policy.
   - Audit and support traces (request IDs, timestamps, routing metadata): visible to Redwood for troubleshooting; full content requires an explicit support authorization.

3) Break-glass: We have a documented break-glass workflow that requires 3 approvals (customer SSO admin + Redwood on-call + privacy officer) and issues an immutable audit record. I'll attach a DPA clause and a sample SOC artifact.

4) Subprocessors/transfers: For private deployments the control plane communications may traverse Redwood-managed endpoints (control plane only); we list subprocessors in the DPA addendum and can geo-fence control plane endpoints to regions. There are no persistent backups stored outside customer-controlled storage unless explicitly configured.

Attached: privdep_operator_matrix.pdf, redwood_dpa_privdep_clause_v1.docx, soc2_type2_sample.pdf

Next steps: Naomi can propose tightened wording for the DPA clause and an operator-visibility SLA. If you want, we can provision a short one-week evidence package for review.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@medicorp.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment boundaries and customer keys

Alice — following Connor's note, attaching a short change to the DPA clause that explicitly enumerates operator entitlements and the break-glass approval flow. Key points here (proposal):

- Customer CMK ownership: clause language ensures the customer retains exclusive control over the CMK and Redwood can only access wrapped keys upon explicit customer:approved unseal request.
- Minimal-visibility operator role: Redwood operators may access only metadata and system telemetry. Any request for content requires a three-party approval (customer admin + Redwood privacy officer + joint legal), logged to an immutable audit trail.
- Break-glass TTL: emergency unsealing is time-limited (max 72 hours) and auto-reseals; all keys used for debug captures are rewrapped under customer CMK and escrowed only if customer opts in.

Suggested snippet for the DPA (plain text to speed review):

"Operator Access: For Private Deployment, Redwood's personnel shall have no routine access to customer plaintext data processed by the Service. Operator actions that may expose data to Redwood personnel are restricted to exceptional events. Exceptional access requires: (1) written customer authorization via the shared ticketing system or an equivalent SSO-approved approval; (2) approval from Redwood's privacy officer; and (3) an automated audit record capturing approver identities, scope, and duration. Any operator-scope debug captures shall be encrypted with the customer's CMK and retain the customer-determined retention period."

I've also added a small table in the attached PDF that maps operator role -> permitted telemetry -> required approvals. Happy to walk through live.

- Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
